=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1060-1072 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `remote_branch_tip()` returns `None` when `git ls-remote` fails, but `_evaluate_mcp_push` handles only `""` and truthy SHA values, so the failure falls through with `tip = ""`.
  WHY: The guard can emit a misleading “no local checkout” reason even when `is_local_checkout` is True, or silently allow a push when ancestry cannot be checked.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1060-1072 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: `remote_branch_tip()` returns `None` when `git ls-remote` fails, but the byte-identical template mirror does not handle that return value explicitly.
  WHY: Consumer repos can receive the same misleading confirmation or unsafe allow behavior when ancestry cannot be checked.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1080-1088 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The `if not tip:` early-return path does not call `_write_cache(slug, branch, pull_requests)` when `cached is None`, discarding freshly fetched PR data.
  WHY: Every subsequent MCP push within the 300-second cache window re-issues the GitHub API request; severity was reported as NIT by three reviewers and MAJOR by one, so the highest severity is used.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1080-1088 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, moonshotai_kimi-k3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The byte-identical template mirror omits `_write_cache(slug, branch, pull_requests)` on the `if not tip:` early-return path.
  WHY: Synced consumer repos repeat the redundant API request for each MCP push within the 300-second cache window; severity was reported as NIT by three reviewers and MAJOR by one, so the highest severity is used.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:the new MCP / verdict test cluster around `test_mcp_push_asks_when_remote_tip_fetch_fails` (lines ~1061-1074 in the new file) | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: The tests cover `fetch_from_origin` returning False but do not cover `remote_branch_tip` returning `None`.
  WHY: A regression in the missing `None` handling can pass CI without verifying that the guard asks for confirmation with an accurate reason; severity was reported as NIT by one reviewer and MAJOR by one, so the highest severity is used.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "Handle `remote_tip is None` explicitly by routing through `_request_confirmation(...)` and returning early, similar to the existing fetch-failure branch (and apply the same change to the workflow-templates mirror to keep copies identical)." (Copilot review comment 3939698589 / 3939698596, echoed by 4 pass-1 reviewers)
  expected_change_site: .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:_evaluate_mcp_push, between the `if remote_tip == "":` block (line 1063) and the `if remote_tip:` block (line 1066); and the byte-identical mirror at workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1063-1066
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  EVIDENCE: The last run diff added `if not fetch_from_origin(...): _request_confirmation(...); return 0, ""` inside the `if remote_tip:` block but did not add the symmetric `if remote_tip is None:` branch. Neither the main hook nor the template mirror contains any check for `remote_tip is None` in the MCP push path. No test covers this case.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1062-1072 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `remote_branch_tip()` returns `None` when `git ls-remote` fails, but only `""` and truthy SHA values are handled, leaving `tip` empty and causing a misleading “without a local checkout” confirmation on a local checkout.
  WHY: The operator may allow a push onto a merged branch based on an incorrect explanation of why ancestry could not be verified.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1080-1088 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The `if not tip:` early-return branch returns without calling `_write_cache(slug, branch, pull_requests)`.
  WHY: Freshly fetched PR data is discarded and repeated MCP pushes re-issue the GitHub API request within the 300-second cache window.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1062-1072 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Same `remote_branch_tip()` `None` handling gap in the byte-identical template mirror.
  WHY: Consumer-repo sessions exhibit the same misleading confirmation text when origin is unreachable from a local checkout.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:1080-1088 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Same `_write_cache` omission in the `if not tip:` early return in the byte-identical template mirror.
  WHY: Consumer-repo sessions doing repeated MCP pushes re-hit the GitHub API within the cache window.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1061-1072 in `_evaluate_mcp_push` (the block beginning `if is_local_checkout: remote_tip = remote_branch_tip(branch, cwd)`); same lines in the byte-identical mirror workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `remote_branch_tip()` returns `None` when `git ls-remote` could not be queried, but the caller handles only `""` and truthy SHA values.
  WHY: The path can emit a misleading “no local checkout” prompt or silently allow a push on a branch whose head is merged-and-absorbed.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1061-1072 in `_evaluate_mcp_push` (same block as the CORRECTNESS finding above); identical mirror workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The autofix added explicit handling for `fetch_from_origin` returning False but not the symmetric explicit handling for `remote_branch_tip` returning `None`.
  WHY: A documented return value falls through to a path whose reason text assumes the wrong preconditions.
- tests/test_pr_merge_status_guard.py:the new MCP / verdict test cluster around `test_mcp_push_asks_when_remote_tip_fetch_fails` (lines ~1061-1074 in the new file) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new tests cover `fetch_from_origin` returning False but have no companion test for `remote_branch_tip` returning `None`.
  WHY: The unfixed branch is covered only by manual reasoning, so a future regression can pass CI.
- workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1079-1089 in `_evaluate_mcp_push` (the `if not tip:` early-return path); identical mirror workflow-templates/.claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: When `tip` is empty, the function returns without calling `_write_cache(slug, branch, pull_requests)`.
  WHY: Every subsequent MCP push re-issues `gh api repos/<slug>/pulls`, inflating API spend in the workflows the cache is intended to protect.
- .claude/hooks/pr_merge_status_guard.py:lines 1063-1067 (the `if not fetch_from_origin(...)` branch added in the last run) and the still-missing symmetric `if remote_tip is None:` branch | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The trust-boundary handling is asymmetric because the `remote_tip is None` case still lacks the ask-and-return guard.
  WHY: An MCP push can either be allowed or receive a misleading prompt when `git ls-remote` fails.
